topic: DEI Programs at Tickle College of Engineering, University of Tennessee
title: DEI Programs at Tickle College of Engineering, University of Tennessee
session_title: Leading and Managing Industry-Academia Collaborations and Partnerships
abstract: Diversity, equity and inclusion is the hallmark of the human experience. To be able to live, worship, cultivate, speak, work, in the company of people from various demographic backgrounds is a privilege. In the Tickle College of Engineering, we strive to ensure ALL stakeholders know that through similarities and differences, respect of people and culture is paramount. Closing in on 50 years of celebrating engineering diversity programs in the College, we are working tirelessly to create sustainable initiatives that mirror the success of our program through the years. We align our priorities with that of the University and College leadership to measure outcomes according to our stakeholders. We are shaping our students, faculty and staff into agents of great intellectual capabilities and understanding that bring all walks of life to the table. Our legacy is strong and incorporating DEI into all of our daily processes continues to make us stronger for the future of the College.

topic: Partnerships Drive UCOR Workplace Recruitment and Retention
title: Partnerships Drive UCOR Workplace Recruitment and Retention
session_title: Leading and Managing Industry-Academia Collaborations and Partnerships
abstract: UCOR, an Amentum-led partnership with Jacobs, is strongly committed to developing the current and future workforce to accomplish the hazardous multi-decade environmental cleanup of land and aging contaminated nuclear facilities on the Department of Energy’s Oak Ridge (TN) Reservation. Successful completion demands well-trained and highly-skilled workers experienced in their discipline or craft and dedicated to safe operations. This presentation will focus on the recruitment, training and retention of the UCOR workforce through multiple avenues, including UCOR in-house training, internships and partnerships with trade unions, regional higher educational institutions, HBCUs, and regional technical schools. Examples include establishment of UCOR’s university consortium, promoting participation in STEM-related fields, and increasing interest by minority students in science and engineering careers.

topic: Siemens' Training Initiative in Developing Modelling Skills for Chemical Engineering Graduates
title: Siemens' Training Initiative in Developing Modelling Skills for Chemical Engineering Graduates
session_title: Leading and Managing Industry-Academia Collaborations and Partnerships
abstract: Digitalization and analytics have become an intrinsic part of industry, which subsequently, has resulted in an increase in the demand for highly skilled professionals. Additionally, novel sustainable technologies require the development of process models that are different from conventional unit operations. These higher requirements for better trained students have put pressure on Chemical Engineering faculties to revisit their academic programmes, in order to ensure that their graduate engineers have the necessary set of skills to face the many challenges in the modern world. There is clear evidence of a gap between what industry requires and expects and what academia can provide. Siemens has been active in bridging this gap by collaborating with universities and facilitating teaching of modelling and simulation in academic programmes. Siemens partners with universities around the world by providing technical content and material that covers different topics such as mass and energy balances, separation methods, thermodynamics, flowsheeting, optimization, among others. This material is modular and flexible so lecturers can incorporate modelling topics throughout the curriculum without taking time away from fundamentals or replacing any other content. Siemens has seen different levels of success with this approach, showing that this effort is a viable and practical way of teaching modelling tools in Chemical Engineering programmes.

topic: Bridge to Bio: Workforce Development in Biopharmaceutical Manufacturing
title: Bridge to Bio: Workforce Development in Biopharmaceutical Manufacturing
session_title: Leading and Managing Industry-Academia Collaborations and Partnerships
abstract: Bridge to Bio is an immersive workforce development program aimed at increasing the diversity of new engineering talent entering the biomanufacturing sector through the Virginia Community College network. A collaboration between the University of Virginia (UVA), Merck, and Pfizer, the program integrates three evidence-based pillars of change: 1) increasing representation, 2) fostering community and belonging, and 3) working to sustain change by building effective industrial relationships. Bridge to Bio began January 2023, with a 5-day immersion program. Fourteen students from across the Virginia Community College network participated in programming that provided insight about how life-saving medicines are manufactured and how to access university engineering programs. Participants also enjoyed a 1-day visit to Merck’s Elkton, VA facility where they received a hands-on experience performing day-to-day manufacturing activities. Keys to program success thus far have been network development, effective messaging, and industry engagement. This presentation will provide an update and a description of the next steps, as well as allow us to share our perspectives on the value of meaningful and effective working relationships with pipeline partners.
